Copy the engine of inlavanilla into a package

Source: R/use-vanilla.R
use_vanilla.Rd

Copies the engine of inlavanilla into the package whose root is path, so that the package can fit models with vanilla_core() and does not need inlavanilla to run. The engine is the code behind inla_vanilla(): the files R/vanilla-*.R of an inlavanilla release. They are copied byte for byte, under the same names, into the package's R/ folder, and listed with their MD5 hashes in the lock inst/inlavanilla.lock.

use_vanilla() also adds to the package's DESCRIPTION what the engine needs, where it is missing:

  • the copyright holders of the engine in Authors@R, with the role "cph", as the DESCRIPTION of inlavanilla at that release lists them;

  • cli (>= 3.6.0), stats and utils in Imports;

  • future and parallelly in Suggests, for the optional parallel scans;

  • R (>= 4.1.0) in Depends, where the package asks for an older R or for none.

It never removes anything, and changes no other file of the package. It prints each change, and ends with a list of what is still to do: any name clashes, the function that calls vanilla_core(), the documentation, the tests, R CMD check and a NEWS bullet.

Run it again with a newer release to update the copy.

Usage

use_vanilla(release = NULL, files = NULL, clone = NULL, path = ".")

Arguments

release

The release of inlavanilla to copy: its tag on GitHub, such as "v26.11.24", or its version, "26.11.24". By default the version of inlavanilla installed here, or, when that version is not a release, the newest release before it.

files

The engine files to copy, as "vanilla-vb.R" or "R/vanilla-vb.R". By default every engine file of the release on a first copy, and the files in the lock on an update (see Details). The engine files call each other, so copy only some of them when you know which you need.

clone

The path of a local clone of inlavanilla, to copy from without the internet. It needs git, and the release tag must be in the clone (git fetch --tags). By default the files come from GitHub.

path

The root of the package, the folder that holds its DESCRIPTION, or a folder inside it. By default the working directory.

Value

Invisibly, a data frame with a row per engine file in the lock: file, its md5 hash, and its state, "new", "restored", "changed" or "unchanged". Its attributes release, commit and previous give the release copied, its commit and the release before it (NA for a first copy), and description and open the changes made to DESCRIPTION and what is still to do, as plain text.

Details

Where the files come from. By default from the release on GitHub, https://github.com/haziqj/inlavanilla, which needs the internet but not git. With clone, from the release tag in a local clone of inlavanilla, which needs git but not the internet. The lock records the release, its commit and the hash of each file, so that vanilla_status() can check the copy later.

Which files. A first copy takes every engine file of the release, or the files in files. An update copies the files in the lock, and adds the files in files, so that every copy comes from one release. It reports the engine files of the release that are not copied, and the ones that the copies need.

A copy edited by hand. When an engine file of the package differs from the lock, use_vanilla() stops and changes nothing, so that the edit is not lost. It also stops for a file R/vanilla-*.R that is not in the lock and differs from the engine file of that name. Never edit an engine file: the next update would undo the edit. Report the problem at https://github.com/haziqj/inlavanilla/issues instead. The names R/vanilla-*.R are kept for the engine, so give your own files other names, and leave the engine files out of any code formatter or linter.

A rights holder already listed. A copyright holder of the engine who is already in Authors@R is not added again. When that entry lacks the role "cph", use_vanilla() leaves it as it is, and lists the role in what is still to do.

License. The engine is under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later, so a package that holds it must be too. use_vanilla() warns when the package's License does not allow that.

vignette("engine", package = "inlavanilla"), also at https://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/engine.html, describes the interface of vanilla_core(), with an example.

See also

vanilla_status() to check the copy, and use_vanilla_test() and use_vanilla_ci() to check it in the tests and on GitHub.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# From the root of your package: copy the engine from the release of the
# inlavanilla installed here
use_vanilla()

# Update the copy to a later release, for example
use_vanilla("v26.12.01")

# Without the internet, from a clone of inlavanilla
use_vanilla(clone = "~/src/inlavanilla")
} # }
